"""SHA-256 of problem['plaintext'].

Calls OpenSSL's AVX2 block function directly on the bytes object's buffer so
there is no Hash-object setup and no input copy. The compression routine is
the same one hashlib/cryptography dispatch to, so this is only slightly faster
at the benchmark size; the digest is standard SHA-256.
"""
import ctypes
import subprocess

_lib = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/lib/libcrypto.3.dylib")


def _file_off(name):
    text = subprocess.check_output(
        ["nm", "/usr/local/lib/libcrypto.3.dylib"],
        text=True,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    )
    for line in text.splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[-1] == name:
            return int(parts[0], 16)
    raise RuntimeError(name)


_base = ctypes.cast(_lib.SHA256, ctypes.c_void_p).value - _file_off("_SHA256")
_compress = ctypes.CFUNCTYPE(None, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t)(
    _base + _file_off("sha256_block_data_order_avx2")
)

# CPython 3.11 PyBytesObject: 32-byte header, then the character data.
_BYTES_HEADER = 32

_IV = (
    0x6A09E667, 0xBB67AE85, 0x3C6EF372, 0xA54FF53A,
    0x510E527F, 0x9B05688C, 0x1F83D9AB, 0x5BE0CD19,
)
_state = (ctypes.c_uint32 * 8)()
_pad = ctypes.create_string_buffer(128)


def _sha256(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    n = len(data)
    nblocks = n >> 6
    rem = n & 63
    st = _state
    st[0], st[1], st[2], st[3], st[4], st[5], st[6], st[7] = _IV
    ptr = id(data) + _BYTES_HEADER
    if nblocks:
        _compress(ctypes.addressof(st), ptr, nblocks)
    if rem:
        ctypes.memmove(_pad, ptr + (nblocks << 6), rem)
    ctypes.memset(ctypes.addressof(_pad) + rem, 0, 128 - rem)
    _pad[rem] = 0x80
    bitlen = n << 3
    if rem >= 56:
        for j in range(8):
            _pad[127 - j] = (bitlen >> (8 * j)) & 0xFF
        _compress(ctypes.addressof(st), ctypes.addressof(_pad), 2)
    else:
        for j in range(8):
            _pad[63 - j] = (bitlen >> (8 * j)) & 0xFF
        _compress(ctypes.addressof(st), ctypes.addressof(_pad), 1)
    out = bytearray(32)
    for i in range(8):
        w = st[i]
        out[4 * i] = (w >> 24) & 0xFF
        out[4 * i + 1] = (w >> 16) & 0xFF
        out[4 * i + 2] = (w >> 8) & 0xFF
        out[4 * i + 3] = w & 0xFF
    return bytes(out)

        return {"digest": _sha256(problem["plaintext"])}

there is no Hash-object setup and no input copy. The compression routine is
the same one hashlib/cryptography dispatch to, so this is only slightly faster

import subprocess

def _file_off(name):
    text = subprocess.check_output(
        ["nm", "/usr/local/lib/libcrypto.3.dylib"],
        text=True,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    )
    for line in text.splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[-1] == name:
            return int(parts[0], 16)
    raise RuntimeError(name)

_compress = ctypes.CFUNCTYPE(None, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t)(
    _base + _file_off("sha256_block_data_order_avx2")
)

# CPython 3.11 PyBytesObject: 32-byte header, then the character data.
_BYTES_HEADER = 32

_IV = (
    0x6A09E667, 0xBB67AE85, 0x3C6EF372, 0xA54FF53A,
    0x510E527F, 0x9B05688C, 0x1F83D9AB, 0x5BE0CD19,
)
_state = (ctypes.c_uint32 * 8)()
_pad = ctypes.create_string_buffer(128)

    n = len(data)
    nblocks = n >> 6
    rem = n & 63
    st = _state
    st[0], st[1], st[2], st[3], st[4], st[5], st[6], st[7] = _IV
    ptr = id(data) + _BYTES_HEADER
    if nblocks:
        _compress(ctypes.addressof(st), ptr, nblocks)
    if rem:
        ctypes.memmove(_pad, ptr + (nblocks << 6), rem)
    ctypes.memset(ctypes.addressof(_pad) + rem, 0, 128 - rem)
    _pad[rem] = 0x80
    bitlen = n << 3

        for j in range(8):
            _pad[127 - j] = (bitlen >> (8 * j)) & 0xFF
        _compress(ctypes.addressof(st), ctypes.addressof(_pad), 2)
    else:

            _pad[63 - j] = (bitlen >> (8 * j)) & 0xFF
        _compress(ctypes.addressof(st), ctypes.addressof(_pad), 1)
    out = bytearray(32)
    for i in range(8):
        w = st[i]
        out[4 * i] = (w >> 24) & 0xFF
        out[4 * i + 1] = (w >> 16) & 0xFF
        out[4 * i + 2] = (w >> 8) & 0xFF
        out[4 * i + 3] = w & 0xFF
    return bytes(out)
